We need to compute P(prize in box1 | opened empty). Model: Prize uniformly among boxes 1-4. You selected box1 but didn't open. Inspector (who doesn't know prize location) chooses uniformly among boxes 2,3,4 to open, independent of prize location. He opens an empty box. Condition on that event.

We need posterior probability that prize is in box1.

Let events: P_i = prize in box i (i=1..4). Inspector selects box J uniformly from {2,3,4}. Then opens it; we observe that opened box is empty (i.e., J != prize location). Since inspector doesn't know location, the probability of opening empty given prize location is: if prize in box1, then any J (2-4) will be empty, because prize not in those boxes. So probability of empty = 1 (since any chosen box is empty). If prize in box k where k∈{2,3,4}, then inspector might choose that same box with probability 1/3, leading to opening prize (not empty). If chooses other box (2/3 chance), opens empty. So conditional probability of empty given prize in box k (k∈{2,3,4}) = 2/3.

Now prior P(P_i) = 1/4 each.

We want P(P_1 | empty) = P(empty | P_1) P(P_1) / P(empty).

Compute numerator: (1)*(1/4)=1/4.

Denominator: sum_i P(empty|P_i)P(P_i)= (1)*(1/4) + 3*(2/3)*(1/4) = 1/4 + 3*(2/3)*(1/4)=1/4 + (3*2/3)*(1/4)=1/4 + (2)*(1/4)=1/4+2/4=3/4.

Thus posterior = (1/4)/(3/4)=1/3.

Thus answer B.
